dispatched_notes: 385th BGA mission summaries (385-02): "Mission No. 28 - 14 October - Target Schweinfurt - 22 a/c flown." AAM mission page (385-10) lists 385BG (21). The 385th BGA Airman DB (385-01) lists 213 airman-sorties in 23 serials, one of which (42-5985) is a single-entry anomaly, giving 22 aircraft. A further 385th airframe, 42-3347 Charlene, was flown by a 96th BG crew (AAM: 96th furnished one crew to the 385th); it was written off on return (crash-landed, out of fuel). Lost = 0 aircraft MIA for 385th crews (no 385th loss on 14 Oct 1943 in 385-03..09; 42-3338 "Sleepy Time Gal", ex-385th, was lost with the 94th BG, MACR 791).

aircraft.loss_details: Battle damaged at Schweinfurt; on return, out of fuel, crash-landed at Bovingdon and salvaged 14/10/43 (AAM 385-03; b17flyingfortress.de 385-11). DISPUTED: a commenter on 385-11 (citing waist gunner Nicolas Popadya, second-hand) says the crew bailed out and the aircraft came down at Rowington, Warwickshire; unconfirmed.
aircraft.notes: 385th BG / 550th BS airframe (code SG-C per 385-11 and AAM) flown by Emery R. Chesmore and a 96th BG crew "+ pass (11 Returned to Duty)" per AAM. AAM mission page (385-10) says the 96th BG furnished one crew to the 385th BG on this mission - very probably this crew. Crew is NOT in the 385th BGA DB (385-01). The 96th BG researcher may also record this sortie; avoid double counting. Only the pilot is named in the aircraft record; AAM also links S/Sgt Clyde Wood Wilkinson (385th/550th waist gunner) to this airframe without a date - not placed on this crew.

crew.name: Emery R. Chesmore

research_gaps: Per-aircraft outcome (bombed vs aborted) not documented: 385th mission report for mission 28 not found online (385-02 gives only "22 a/c flown"). 385th BGA mission-report PDFs were not located for this mission.

Position detail incomplete: 385-01 often gives only "G" (gunner) without station; engineers are mostly not distinguished from gunners.
